plan_steps: Step 1 (PLAN): Define analysis objectives and data requirements. Establish that we will categorize all 47 transactions by merchant and transaction type, identify spending patterns in food supplier accounts (Sysco Foods and US Foods), calculate daily/weekly averages, and determine cash flow impact. Set benchmarks to evaluate if spending is aligned with startup operational needs and typical food service industry standards.

Step 2 (ACT): Execute transaction categorization and computation. Process all 47 transactions across the October 2024 date range, segment spending by merchant (primary focus on Sysco Foods and US Foods), calculate weekly totals and per-transaction averages, identify transaction frequency and timing patterns, and compute total monthly debit outflows versus any credit inflows to establish net cash position.

Step 3 (OBSERVE): Examine processed data for patterns and anomalies. Note that Sysco Foods represents 4 transactions totaling $16,921.05 (approximately $4,230 weekly average), US Foods shows 1 transaction of $2,340.15, identify the 7-day transaction cycle for Sysco, flag whether remaining 42 transactions follow similar supplier concentration patterns, observe any unusual spike dates or merchant diversity, and document the overall cash burn rate from food supplier spending.

Step 4 (SUMMARIZE): Consolidate findings into actionable insights. Present total food supplier spending ($19,261.20 from visible data), highlight that Sysco Foods dominates the food cost category with consistent weekly ordering, calculate the implied monthly run-rate based on October patterns, compare supplier concentration risk (heavy reliance on Sysco), and provide a clear statement of whether current spending appears sustainable for a startup operation with associated cash runway implications.

Step 5 (REFLECT): Evaluate analysis quality and recommend next steps. Assess whether the 5-transaction sample represents typical startup food service spending or signals potential waste, identify data gaps (need to review remaining 42 transactions and any credit deposits), recommend cost optimization opportunities through supplier diversification or volume consolidation, suggest implementing spending thresholds or approval workflows, and propose monthly variance analysis to track actual-vs-budget performance going forward.
